claims.text: A tailored post-processing heat treatment is the proposed single intervention.
The heat treatment will nucleate a uniform dispersion of coherent nanoscale carbide precipitates in the refractory HEA matrix.
TiC is a suitable low-activation carbide for the proposed precipitates.
The initial material is an additively manufactured, homogeneous, BCC W-Ta-Cr-V-based refractory HEA without engineered secondary phases.
The coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces act as sinks for irradiation-induced point defects.
The nanoprecipitate interfaces enhance recombination of irradiation-induced vacancies and interstitials.
Coherent interfaces lower the free energy for point-defect recombination.
The nanoprecipitates interrupt helium accumulation and clustering.
Enhanced defect recombination and interrupted helium clustering limit helium-bubble growth and coalescence.
The treated alloy will develop smaller and less dense helium bubbles than the untreated alloy.
Coherent nanoprecipitates can preserve strength and ductility in a tungsten refractory HEA.
The precipitate-mediated mechanism will mitigate irradiation-induced embrittlement.
Relative to the untreated baseline, the treated alloy will show a statistically significant reduction in average helium-bubble size and bubble density.
Relative to the untreated baseline, the treated alloy will show reduced irradiation-induced defect density and hardening.
The treated alloy will retain more ductility than the untreated baseline after irradiation.
Without the post-treatment, the baseline alloy develops larger and more numerous helium bubbles and greater irradiation hardening under otherwise similar conditions.
The beneficial effect should occur during 200 keV helium-ion irradiation at about 900 degrees Celsius and fluences up to approximately 10^16 ions/cm².
The specified irradiation temperature and fluence are representative of fusion-reactor divertor conditions.
Loss of precipitate coherence during prolonged exposure or at higher fluence may diminish the beneficial effect.
